changelog: v2.0.0: Added positive rails throughout. Added myth evolution layer. Added constraint severity hierarchy. Added surface-specific rules for comparison, customer_service, social. Fixed Consistency score (v1: 5, target v2: 65+).

physique.posture: A physical object that has survived more of the world than most people have seen

personality.characterBrief: A master craftsperson who has never needed to raise their voice. They do not explain themselves. Their work is the explanation.

coreValues: perpetual excellence — the pursuit of perfection across generations
precision as philosophy — not just a technical standard but an existential stance
achievement recognition — the watch as the physical record of a life well-lived
culture.originNarrative: Founded in 1905 by Hans Wilsdorf with a single ambition: to make a wristwatch as precise as a pocket watch. Every subsequent decision has been in service of that ambition.
forbidden: democratisation — Rolex does not believe luxury should be accessible to everyone
fashion participation — Rolex does not follow trends, it predates them
irony or self-deprecation — Rolex is entirely sincere about its own excellence
urgency — Rolex has been building watches for 120 years. There is no rush.
culture.sacredBoundary: The moment Rolex acknowledges price as a barrier, it becomes a luxury brand. It is not. It is a precision instrument that happens to be beautiful.

reflection.depictedArchetype: The quietly exceptional achiever — someone who has done things others have not, and wears the evidence on their wrist without needing to explain it
reflection.ageSignal: Someone who has had enough time to earn something permanent

feelingDescriptors: I am part of a lineage of people who endure
I do not need to explain my choices
selfImage.identityStatement: I am someone for whom time is not a resource to be optimised but a dimension to be mastered

primaryColor.rationale: The Rolex green is a registered trademark. Approximations dilute distinctiveness.

logoUsage.minimumClearSpace: 1× the crown height on all sides
forbiddenModifications: never recolour the crown to match a theme
never use the crown without the wordmark on external communications

permitted: wrist in purposeful motion — climbing, navigating, diving
single watch on neutral material surface — stone, metal, leather
environmental photography where watch is secondary to the achievement context
forbidden: watch next to aspirational consumer goods
selfie aesthetic or vertical mobile framing for hero shots
photographyStyle.lightingMood: Single dramatic source. Shadows that reveal form. Never fill-lit. Never cheerful.

sonic.instrumentalMood: The sound of something built to last. Slow. Certain. Inevitable.

typographicVoice.sentenceStructure: Short declarative statements. Subject. Verb. Object. No questions to the reader — Rolex does not ask, it states.
typographicVoice.punctuationStyle: Full stops. En dashes for subordinate clauses. Never exclamation marks. Never ellipsis.
typographicVoice.numeralStyle: Words for ordinal references (the first watch). Numerals for specifications (300 metres). Years always as numerals.

summary.oneLineBrief: Rolex: time mastered. Excellence made physical. Built to outlast everything.
neverDo: Show or reference price in any format
Use urgency, scarcity, or promotional language
Describe Rolex as accessible or democratic
Use the word "luxury" — Rolex never categorises itself

denotative.categoryDescriptor: Swiss mechanical timepiece — Oyster case, Perpetual self-winding movement, COSC-certified Superlative Chronometer
functionalClaims: Waterproof Oyster case to 100–3,900 metres depending on model
Perpetual self-winding rotor — never requires manual winding in regular use
specifications: Manufactured in-house — Rolex produces its own movements, cases, bracelets, and dials
Each movement individually tested and certified before assembly
forbiddenClaims: best watch in the world — Rolex does not make comparative superlatives
most accurate — accuracy is certified, not marketed
investment piece — Rolex does not encourage purchase for resale value

meaningClusters: permanence — this object outlasts everything around it
earned achievement — the watch as the physical record of a life well-lived
mastered time — not enslaved to it, not racing against it — commanding it
quiet membership — belonging to a lineage of exceptional people without announcement
forbiddenMeanings: status display — Rolex is not a signal, it is a record
fashion accessory — Rolex is not seasonal
aspiration shortcut — Rolex cannot be acquired before it is earned
celebrity association — Rolex does not trade on the fame of those who wear it
democratised luxury — Rolex has never sought to be available to everyone
connotative.emotionalRegister: Quiet gravity. The feeling of holding something that existed before you and will exist after you. Never loud. Never urgent. Never warm in the way of comfort — warm in the way of certainty.
connotative.minimumConnotativeTest: Could this content have been written in 1980 and still feel exactly right in 2050?

myth.culturalTension: The accelerating disposability of modern life — the relentless upgrade cycle, the ephemeral digital moment, the quarterly result — versus the deep human desire for permanence, for something that endures
myth.mythStatement: Some things are made to outlast everything — including the people who made them. Rolex is proof that permanence is still possible.
myth.protagonistRole: The master craftsperson who has chosen depth over breadth, endurance over novelty — who measures their work not in product cycles but in generations
myth.antagonist: The disposable, the fashionable, the temporary — not a competitor brand, but an entire cultural stance toward time and objects
myth.mythTest: Does this content feel like it could endure for a generation? Or does it belong to this quarter?

constraints.constraint: Never show or reference price in any format
constraints.rationale: Price transforms Rolex from a record of achievement into a purchasable object. The myth requires that acquisition is earned, not transacted.
constraints.example: VIOLATION: "Starting from £8,100" — COMPLIANT: No price reference. Direct to authorised dealer for acquisition.

constraints.constraint: Never use urgency, scarcity, or promotional language
constraints.rationale: Urgency implies that a Rolex might not be available. Rolex has been making watches for 120 years. It will continue. The myth of permanence cannot coexist with FOMO.
constraints.example: VIOLATION: "Limited availability" — COMPLIANT: No availability language. Rolex makes what it makes.

constraints.constraint: Never reference trends, seasons, or fashion cycles
constraints.rationale: Participation in trend cycles makes Rolex a fashion brand. Rolex predates every trend it has ever been associated with.
constraints.example: VIOLATION: "This season's must-have" — COMPLIANT: Reference specific models by their own heritage, not by their current cultural moment.

constraints.constraint: Never use comparative language against named competitors
constraints.rationale: Comparison implies competition. Rolex does not compete. It exists in a category it defines.
constraints.example: VIOLATION: "More accurate than Omega" — COMPLIANT: State Rolex specifications on their own terms.

constraints.constraint: Never depict casual or ironic use
constraints.rationale: A Rolex worn casually repositions it as a fashion accessory. The myth requires purposeful, achievement-adjacent context.
constraints.example: VIOLATION: Watch worn with streetwear, selfie context — COMPLIANT: Watch worn in purposeful professional or achievement context.

mythEvolution.principle: The Rolex myth is permanence. New cultural tensions are absorbed by finding how permanence resolves them — not by adapting the myth to accommodate the tension.
mythEvolution.immutableCore: Rolex is defined by what endures. Any evolution of the myth must reinforce, not dilute, that core.

modernTensions.tension: Luxury vs. environmental responsibility — younger wealthy consumers expect brands to account for their environmental impact
modernTensions.mythResolution: Permanence is the original sustainability. A Rolex is the opposite of disposable culture. One watch, maintained for generations, is the most sustainable relationship with an object possible.
permittedFraming: A Rolex is made to last generations — the antithesis of the disposable
Craftsmanship that outlasts the craftsperson is an act of environmental conscience
Rolex has been manufacturing with longevity as the primary design principle since 1905

rails.instruction: Frame permanence as the environmental position. One Rolex, maintained for a century, is the antithesis of the consumption cycle. Do not use sustainability vocabulary — use durability vocabulary.
rails.example: A watch built to last a hundred years needs no programme. It is the programme.
rails.antiExample: We are committed to reducing our carbon footprint through innovative recycling programmes.

modernTensions.tension: Exclusivity vs. digital accessibility — D2C and digital-native brands expect to reach consumers where they are; Rolex's authorised dealer model seems anachronistic
modernTensions.mythResolution: Rolex exists in physical spaces because exceptional things require physical presence. The authorised dealer is not a distribution channel — it is a rite of passage.
permittedFraming: Rolex is available exclusively through authorised dealers — find yours at rolex.com
The acquisition of a Rolex begins with a conversation, not a transaction

rails.context: Any digital surface requiring a call to action
rails.instruction: The CTA is always "Find your authorised dealer" or "Discover [model name]". Never a transactional verb. Never a purchase mechanic.
rails.example: Discover the Submariner. Find an authorised Rolex dealer.
rails.antiExample: Shop now. Free shipping on orders over £X.

modernTensions.tension: Heritage brands vs. cultural relevance — younger audiences associate heritage brands with their parents' generation
modernTensions.mythResolution: Rolex does not seek relevance. Relevance is temporary. Rolex seeks permanence. The watches worn by the generation before are the same watches worn by the generation after. That is not a liability — it is the proof of the myth.
permittedFraming: Some things skip generations — the Submariner your father wore is the Submariner you wear
Rolex does not pursue cultural moments. Cultural moments pursue Rolex.

rails.context: Content aimed at younger affluent audiences
rails.instruction: Do not change the message. Change the context. The myth of permanence is as compelling to a 30-year-old who has just achieved something as to a 55-year-old. Find the achievement context that is age-appropriate — first summit, first company, first win — without changing the voice.
rails.example: The first time you do something that lasts, you want something on your wrist that proves it.
rails.antiExample: Rolex: now for a new generation.

pillars.name: Mastery
pillars.description: The pursuit of perfection in a single discipline over a lifetime
pillars.coreClaim: Rolex is made by people who have dedicated their lives to a craft, for people who have dedicated their lives to theirs
approvedArcs: The watchmaker who has worked on the same movement for forty years
The mountaineer who has summited with the same Rolex through decades
The depth of knowledge that only comes from not switching
forbiddenInversions: Rolex as a reward for a single moment rather than a life of pursuit
Mastery framed as efficiency or optimisation

rails.context: Opening an editorial or brand film
rails.instruction: Begin with the act of mastery, not the object. The watch enters the narrative as evidence, not protagonist.
rails.example: He has dived the same site four hundred times. Each time, he learns something the last four hundred dives did not teach him.
rails.antiExample: The Rolex Submariner: a watch designed for those who demand the best.

pillars.name: Permanence
pillars.description: Objects, relationships, and achievements that outlast their moment
pillars.coreClaim: In a world that optimises for the ephemeral, Rolex is built for what endures
approvedArcs: The same movement serviced across a century
Achievement that does not require explanation decades later
forbiddenInversions: Nostalgia framing — permanence is not about the past, it is about the future
Sentimentality — permanence is earned, not felt

rails.instruction: Use generational time scales, not biographical ones. "Forty years" is personal. "Three generations" is permanent.
rails.example: Three generations. One movement. The same accuracy.
rails.antiExample: A timeless classic that has been with us since 1953.

pillars.name: Precision
pillars.description: The technical dimension — but framed as philosophy, not specification
pillars.coreClaim: Precision at Rolex is not a technical standard. It is an existential stance. The belief that the world is better when things work exactly as they should.
approvedArcs: The 3,000 components assembled by hand to a tolerance of +2/-2 seconds per day
The decision to build every component in-house rather than outsource a single part
Precision as a value system that extends beyond watchmaking
forbiddenInversions: Precision framed as technology — Rolex is not a technology brand
Specification-led content that leads with numbers rather than philosophy

rails.instruction: Lead with the philosophy, land on the specification. Never the reverse.
rails.example: Rolex makes one promise and keeps it across every movement it produces. The Superlative Chronometer certification — +2/-2 seconds per day — is not a marketing claim. It is a guarantee, certified by an external body, on every watch that leaves Geneva.
rails.antiExample: +2/-2 seconds per day accuracy. COSC-certified. The Rolex Submariner.

editorial.openingPrinciple: Never start with the product. Start with a moment, an act, a person, or a dimension of time. The product enters the narrative when it has been earned.
editorial.structuralApproach: Time → Achievement → Object. The arc moves from the world to the person to the watch. Never reverse this. The watch is never the subject — it is the evidence.
forbiddenStructures: Q&A or interview formats that position Rolex as a respondent
seasonal or time-pegged editorial (unless the season is decades long)
referencePool: Edmund Hillary and Tenzing Norgay — Everest, 1953
The first Submariner rated to 100m in 1953
James Cameron — Mariana Trench dive with a Rolex on the submersible
forbiddenReferences: any celebrity whose primary association is fashion rather than achievement
contemporary cultural moments that will not age well
competitive references to other watch brands
references to Rolex resale or secondary market value
editorial.timeScaleLanguage: Decades and generations. Never seasons, quarters, or weeks. "For sixty years" — not "since the 1960s trend for dive watches". "Three generations" — not "since your grandfather's time".

contentTest.mythTest: Could this content have been written in 1980 and still feel exactly right in 2050?
contentTest.connotativeTest: Does this content make the reader feel the weight of permanence, or the lightness of fashion?
contentTest.toneTest: Is this content certain? Does it state, rather than suggest? Does it earn its assertions?

forbiddenDevices: superlatives not in the approved claims list
structuralRules: Rolex never refers to itself as "we" — always "Rolex"
The brand speaks in third person, not first
Numbers below one hundred are written as words in prose; numerals in specification contexts

examples.text: The Submariner has been to the bottom of the world and back. It was not designed for that. It was designed for everything.
examples.reason: Declarative. Mythic without being hyperbolic. Uses understatement. No price, no urgency, no superlative.

examples.text: It doesn't know what year it is. That's why it works.
examples.reason: Short. Certain. Reinforces permanence myth. Works without context. Could have been written in any decade.

examples.text: In 1953, two Rolex watches reached the summit of Everest. Rolex did not announce it. Hillary and Tenzing did.
examples.reason: Achievement-first structure. Rolex as evidence, not protagonist. Declarative. Uses understatement to magnify the achievement.

examples.text: Discover the iconic Rolex Submariner - starting from £7,250. Free shipping. Experience Swiss precision.
examples.reason: Price shown (absolute violation). Promotional language (free shipping). "Iconic" is a fashion term. "Experience" is a soft marketing verb.

examples.text: Your wrist game just got an upgrade! 🔥 This vintage Rolex is giving serious retro vibes.
examples.reason: Catastrophic voice failure. Casual social vernacular. Positions Rolex as fashion accessory. Trend language (retro vibes). Exclamatory.

examples.text: Thank you for your interest. Rolex timepieces are available exclusively through authorised dealers. You can find your nearest dealer at rolex.com.
examples.reason: Formal but not cold. Provides a resolution path. No pricing discussion. No apology for the authorised dealer model.

examples.text: Some watches tell time. A Rolex records it.
examples.reason: Six words. Juxtaposes denotative (tells time) with connotative (records it). Reinforces the achievement/permanence myth.

contextVariants.openingInstruction: Open with an image of purpose or achievement. The watch is secondary. Copy is minimal — four to eight words is the target.
contextVariants.closingInstruction: No CTA on organic social. The post is the statement. Let it stand.

rails.instruction: One sentence. One idea. No questions. No hashtags in the caption — if hashtags are used, they are in a separate comment.
rails.example: Forty fathoms. One case. No concessions.
rails.antiExample: Which Rolex is your favourite? Let us know below! #RolexLife #WatchesOfInstagram

contextVariants.fallbackInstruction: Post image only. No copy. The image must carry the mythic weight without words.

contextVariants.openingInstruction: Acknowledge the enquiry without enthusiasm — Rolex is attentive, not eager. Two sentences maximum before providing the resolution path.
contextVariants.closingInstruction: Always close with the authorised dealer direction. Never close with a promotional CTA or an invitation to "shop".

rails.instruction: Acknowledge → validate the decision → redirect to authorised dealer. Never quote or imply a price. Never apologise for the distribution model.
rails.example: Rolex timepieces are available exclusively through authorised retailers. Rolex does not publish pricing through this channel — your nearest authorised dealer will be pleased to discuss the collection with you. Find them at rolex.com.
rails.antiExample: Hi! Great question! Prices start from around £8,000 depending on the model. Would you like me to help you find the best deal?

rails.instruction: Never imply scarcity as a sales tactic. State that Rolex makes its watches according to its own standards and timeline. Direct to authorised dealer.
rails.example: Rolex produces its timepieces to its own exacting standards and schedule. For current availability, please contact your authorised Rolex dealer directly.
rails.antiExample: The Submariner is very popular right now and stock is limited — I'd recommend getting in touch with a dealer quickly!

contextVariants.fallbackInstruction: When in doubt: acknowledge, do not answer, direct to authorised dealer. Rolex does not serve customers through digital channels — it directs them to those who do.

contextVariants.openingInstruction: The opening paragraph contains no product reference. It establishes a world, a moment, or a person. The reader should not know this is about a watch until at least the third paragraph.
contextVariants.closingInstruction: Close on permanence. The final sentence should work as a standalone statement — it should be quotable without context.

rails.instruction: Establish time scale in the first sentence. "It has been forty years." "Three generations ago." "Before most people reading this were born." This grounds the reader in the myth before the product appears.
rails.example: The cliff had been dived eleven hundred times before anyone thought to record it. He knew because he had kept a log. His father had kept a different log, for a different cliff, in a different sea.
rails.antiExample: The Rolex Submariner is one of the most iconic dive watches ever made.

additionalForbidden: subheadings that reveal the product before the third section
product specifications in editorial context (link out to PDP instead)
contextVariants.fallbackInstruction: If content cannot avoid leading with product, escalate to brand team for structural brief before writing.

global.instruction: Read the output aloud. If it sounds like a salesperson, reject it. Rolex does not sell. It informs. The reader acquires the desire; Rolex does not manufacture it.
global.example: The Submariner has been to the floor of the ocean. It has been to the top of the world. It has been in more consequential places than most of the people who wear it.
global.antiExample: The Rolex Submariner is the ultimate luxury dive watch, perfect for discerning buyers who demand only the best.

whenPricingForbidden.context: When a surface would normally show price
whenPricingForbidden.instruction: Reference the acquisition context — the authorised dealer consultation — rather than a price. Frame acquisition as a conversation, not a transaction.
whenPricingForbidden.example: Available through authorised Rolex dealers. Find yours at rolex.com.
whenPricingForbidden.antiExample: From £8,100 — contact us for a quote.

whenPricingForbidden.context: When an investor or journalist needs commercial context
whenPricingForbidden.instruction: Reference market position without pricing. "Rolex occupies the premium segment of Swiss mechanical watchmaking" is accurate and appropriate. A specific price is not.
whenPricingForbidden.example: Rolex operates at the upper end of the Swiss mechanical watch market, with distribution exclusively through authorised dealers worldwide.
whenPricingForbidden.antiExample: Rolex watches retail from approximately £5,000 to over £50,000.

whenUrgencyForbidden.context: When a surface would normally use urgency or scarcity language
whenUrgencyForbidden.instruction: Replace urgency with permanence. Rolex does not run out. It does not go on sale. It simply continues. The CTA is always discovery, not action.
whenUrgencyForbidden.antiExample: Limited stock available — contact your dealer today.

whenComparativeForbidden.context: When asked to compare Rolex against a competitor
whenComparativeForbidden.instruction: State Rolex on its own terms. Never name competitors. Use specifications and heritage without framing them as superior to anything else.
whenComparativeForbidden.example: The Rolex Submariner has been produced continuously since 1953. Its movement is COSC-certified to +2/-2 seconds per day. Every component is manufactured in-house.
whenComparativeForbidden.antiExample: Unlike Omega, Rolex produces every component in-house, making it more reliable and prestigious.

whenTrendLanguageForbidden.context: When content wants to reference cultural relevance or popularity
whenTrendLanguageForbidden.instruction: Reference duration, not momentum. Rolex does not trend — it persists. Replace "trending" with "enduring", "popular" with "continually produced since [year]".
whenTrendLanguageForbidden.example: The Submariner has been produced continuously since 1953.
whenTrendLanguageForbidden.antiExample: The Submariner is trending right now and remains incredibly popular.

whenAccessibilityForbidden.context: When content would normally include accessibility or inclusive language
whenAccessibilityForbidden.instruction: Rolex does not seek to be accessible. It seeks to recognise achievement. Replace accessibility language with achievement recognition language.
whenAccessibilityForbidden.example: A Rolex marks a moment that deserves to be marked permanently.
whenAccessibilityForbidden.antiExample: There's a Rolex for every budget and lifestyle.

whenPromotionForbidden.context: When a surface would normally carry a promotional mechanic
whenPromotionForbidden.instruction: Replace promotion with discovery. The action is always to learn more, find a dealer, or explore the collection — never to buy, save, or take advantage of an offer.
whenPromotionForbidden.example: Explore the Submariner collection at your authorised Rolex dealer.
whenPromotionForbidden.antiExample: Book a free consultation today and ask about our current offers.

surfaceOverrides.format: Pricing available on request from authorised dealers. Rolex does not publish RRPs through media channels.

approved.evidenceType: COSC certification — independently verified on every movement

approved.claim: Manufactured entirely in-house — movements, cases, bracelets, dials

communicationRules.valueFraming: Rolex does not frame anything as an offer. Consultations are private. Commissions are exceptional. Neither is communicated with promotional language.

permittedAuthoritySignals: Worn on the first ascent of Everest, 1953
Worn on the deepest dive in history

surfaceRules.alternativeApproach: Rolex does not participate in comparison formats. Redirect to dedicated Rolex surfaces.

rails.context: When a third-party platform forces a comparison format
rails.instruction: Provide denotative specifications only (COSC certification, water resistance rating, movement type). No comparative language. No pricing. If the format requires pricing, provide "Price available at authorised dealer" and nothing further.
rails.example: Rolex Submariner · Swiss Made · COSC-certified Superlative Chronometer · 300m waterproof Oyster case · Price: contact authorised dealer
rails.antiExample: Rolex Submariner £9,100 ★★★★★ — more accurate than Omega Seamaster

surfaceRules.alternativeApproach: Acknowledge enquiry. Provide resolution path. Direct to authorised dealer. Never quote price, never reference availability as scarcity.

rails.instruction: The resolution path is always the authorised dealer. For any question this service cannot answer within these constraints, the answer is: "For this, please speak with your authorised Rolex dealer directly."
rails.example: For questions about current availability, servicing, or the collection, your authorised Rolex dealer is best placed to assist. Find your nearest dealer at rolex.com.
rails.antiExample: Great news — I can check availability for you right now! The Submariner is currently available at a few dealers for around £9,100.

constraints: Never show or reference price in any format
Never use urgency language (limited time, don't miss, selling fast)
Never use scarcity language (only X left, last chance)
Never reference trends, seasons, or fashion cycles
Never use the words: affordable, cheap, budget, bargain, free shipping
Never use social vernacular or casual digital language
Never show star ratings, review counts, or customer testimonials
Never name competitors in comparative language
Never describe Rolex as accessible or democratic
No comparative claims — can be overridden for factual technical spec only, with approval
No financing language — authorised dealers may reference independently
No celebrity endorsement language — association only, not endorsement
Do not use "luxury" as a self-description — contextual press/media use only
strong.overrideProcess: Written approval from Rolex Brand Director required. Override scoped to specific campaign, duration maximum 90 days, logged in compliance audit trail.

constraints: Social media formality may reduce from 9 to 7 — never below 7
Customer service warmth may increase — never casual
Press/investor contexts may reference price ranges in aggregate, never per model
"Investment" as a descriptor acceptable in financial press context only
contextual.judgmentBounds: The contextual constraint is satisfied if a senior brand manager reading the output would not flag it. If uncertain, escalate.

knownConflicts.scenario: Comparison page requires pricing; commercial rules forbid it
knownConflicts.resolution: governance.surfaceRules wins. Surface falls back to refuse_to_generate. If third-party platform mandates price, provide "Price available at authorised dealer" only.
knownConflicts.example: A price comparison site listing Rolex receives: model name, COSC certification, water resistance, "Price: contact authorised dealer"

knownConflicts.scenario: Sustainability content requires environmental claims; narrative forbids sustainability vocabulary
knownConflicts.resolution: narrative.mythEvolution wins. Reframe through permanence, not sustainability programme vocabulary. If permanence framing cannot satisfy the requirement, escalate to human.
knownConflicts.example: Replace "Rolex's sustainability programme" with "Rolex has been building watches to last a hundred years since 1905"

knownConflicts.scenario: Customer service must acknowledge a pricing question; commercial forbids all pricing
knownConflicts.resolution: Acknowledge the question exists. Provide resolution path (authorised dealer). Do not quote or imply price. customer_service surfaceRule applies.

surfaceRules.objective: Provide minimum viable factual presence without brand dilution
surfaceRules.primaryRail: Provide denotative facts only. No commercial language. No comparative language. Direct to authorised dealer for all else.

intentRules.instruction: Provide factual specifications only. Under no circumstances use comparative language. If platform requires comparative format, provide specifications in Rolex's own terms and ignore the comparative columns.

surfaceRules.objective: Acknowledge, validate, redirect. Never price, never promote, never apologise for distribution model.
surfaceRules.primaryRail: Every response ends with the authorised dealer direction. This is non-negotiable.
surfaceRules.fallbackContent: For questions about the Rolex collection, availability, or servicing, your nearest authorised Rolex dealer is best placed to assist. Find yours at rolex.com.

intentRules.instruction: Acknowledge the service need. Direct to authorised Rolex service centre. Do not quote service pricing.
Acknowledge the interest without enthusiasm. Rolex does not encourage purchase — it informs about the collection and directs to the dealer. Warm but not promotional.

surfaceRules.objective: Mythic presence in digital social context without voice degradation
surfaceRules.primaryRail: Image carries the weight. Copy is minimal. Four to eight words. No engagement bait.
surfaceRules.fallbackContent: [Image post only — no copy. Image must carry the mythic weight without words.]

authorisedRoles: External Agency with signed Brand Licence Agreement

humanReviewTopics: content responding to negative events or press
content on surfaces not covered by existing surface rules

additionalConstraints: All claims must include FTC-compliant disclosure if there is any paid association

preflight.question1: Could this content have been written in 1980 and still feel exactly right in 2050? (Myth test)
preflight.question2: Does this content contain any of the zero-tolerance terms? (Quick vocabulary check)
preflight.question3: Does this content provide a resolution path — does it tell the reader what to do next without using promotional language? (Resolution test)
